Marc —

Thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. Short update below and next steps.

Legal redlines (egress / data retention):
- We reviewed Crestview's suggested carveouts in §7.2. The core platform position is to retain data for operational debugging and SLO purposes (default retention 30 days for request logs, 90 days for trace logs) but we can offer a customer-specific retention policy and an export/egress window.
- Proposed compromise: Add a defined export window (up to 30 days) and an encrypted-delivery clause for egress. We will not retain customer-uploaded PHI beyond the customer's specified retention period if requested in the Order Form.
- I've asked Kimberly to provide recommended redline language that preserves our auditability requirements while addressing your egress concern.

Portal gating / Ariba checklist:
- We can support EDI (X12), PO acknowledgement (POACK) within a 24–48h ack window, and SFTP for batch EDI. We also support API-based webhook delivery for real-time PO events if preferred.
- Critical fields: Vendor legal name, remit_to_address, tax_id (TIN/EIN), vendor_site_code, preferred_invoice_format (edi/pdf), PO_ack_window (24h default), invoice_match_tolerance (3%), GL_segment (if required).
- Action item: Ben will map the Crestview workbook fields to our activation profile and return a filled mapping table by EOD Friday.

Timeline: if we close legal redlines this week and Ben returns the mapping, we can provision Ariba credentials and complete EDI/SFTP tests by Dec 8.

Next steps:
1) Kimberly: redline suggestion for §7.2 (see note below).
2) Ben: field mapping to Crestview workbook and EDI transport selection.
3) Marc/Aisha: confirm preferred transport (SFTP vs webhook) and any exceptions to retention.

I'll keep this thread as the canonical thread.

—Lauren Bishop

Team / Marc —

I reviewed Crestview's v3 redlines and drafted alternate language. Main points:
1) Egress/export window: suggested language — 'Customer may request export of Customer Data within thirty (30) days following termination; Redwood will provide a machine-readable encrypted export within this period. Following export, Redwood may delete residual Customer Data except audit logs required to meet legal obligations.'
2) PHI handling: we can accept a statement that the customer is responsible for de-identifying data prior to upload unless a BAA is executed. For PHI-specific deployments, we recommend a Private deployment option (VPC/on-prem) — but operationally we will add an appendix for processing scope.
3) Liability cap: we can accept a limited liability for direct damages up to the aggregate fees paid in the prior 12 months; we cannot accept open-ended consequential damages.

I've attached a pdf with inline suggested edits (Crestview_MSA_redlines_v3_suggested.pdf). If Crestview wants any of these moved to the Order Form as a deployable option (e.g., longer egress window, extended retention) we can do that and keep the MSA lean.

I recommend:
- Lauren responds with our suggested wording and asks procurement whether they want any items as Order Form options.
- If Crestview wants the longer egress or a formal BAA, we route to the Private deployment sales path.

--Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
